stem: On a map of the Earth seen from above the North Pole, there are circles around the pole and lines radiating out from it. What are these lines?
options: Circles are meridians; radiating lines are parallels of latitude
Circles are ocean boundaries; radiating lines are ocean currents
Circles are time zones; radiating lines mark the two hemispheres
Circles are parallels of latitude; radiating lines are meridians
explanation: Correct option: (D). Parallels of latitude run around the Earth as circles, so seen from above a pole they appear as rings around it. Meridians of longitude run from pole to pole, so they appear as lines radiating out of the pole. Swapping the two is a common mistake, and the lines do not mark ocean boundaries, currents or time zones.
